title: Ivo and the Orchard
premise: In 1848, apprentice clockmaker Wendell Dravenmoor is summoned to the hilltop observatory to repair its failing master clock, only to discover the town's founding families have been quietly rewriting their history to erase the orchard-keepers who built it. When a sealed letter from a dying archivist names the Dravenmoor family among the erased, Wendell must choose between the comfortable apprenticeship he's been promised and the truth no one wants recorded. Racing the victors' hired historians and the town's most powerful men, he restores the master clock to reveal the original records hidden in its mechanism, forcing the town to reckon publicly with its past. The book ends with Wendell refusing the apprenticeship, staying to rebuild the orchard with the found family of keepers and archivists who claim him.
about_author: Coral Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing provincial records before turning to fiction. Her work explores what ordinary people carry when institutions decide what history is worth keeping.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Wendell, POV, finishes a pocket watch in his master's cramped workshop and reflects on measuring life in portable things. He is summoned by letter to the observatory. Emotional beat: quiet ambition shadowed by the knowledge that apprentices are always replaceable.

chapters.title: The Hill Road
chapters.summary: Wendell travels to the observatory town of Marrowgate, noticing the orchards on the hillsides are untended and the keepers' cottages abandoned. A farmer warns him not to ask questions. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: unease beneath the beauty of the landscape.

chapters.title: The Master Clock
chapters.summary: Wendell meets the observatory's aging caretaker, Bram Tull, and examines the great clock, finding deliberate sabotage rather than wear. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: professional pride curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Founders' Hall
chapters.summary: Wendell is received by Alderman Corvus Hale, who is charming and generous, and offers Wendell a permanent post if the clock is fixed quietly. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: flattered, but the offer feels like a bribe.

chapters.title: The Sealed Letter
chapters.summary: Bram gives Wendell a sealed letter from the late archivist Odile Fen, to be opened only if the clock's mechanism resists repair. POV: Bram's for the first third, then Wendell's. Emotional beat: dread passed like an inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Letter Named
chapters.summary: Wendell opens the letter: it names the Dravenmoor family as orchard-keepers erased from Marrowgate's founding records, and claims the original registry is hidden inside the master clock. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the ground tilting under him.

chapters.title: The Empty Cottages
chapters.summary: Wendell walks the abandoned orchard terraces and finds a cottage with his own surname carved on the lintel. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: grief for a family he never knew he had.

chapters.title: The Historian Arrives
chapters.summary: A polished historian, Mr. Lachlan Vey, arrives under Hale's patronage to write the official town history. He interviews Wendell with friendly, probing questions. POV: Vey's, briefly, then Wendell's. Emotional beat: being measured by a man who erases.

chapters.title: Gears and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wendell begins secretly examining the clock's inner casing at night, finding a false compartment he cannot open without destroying the escapement. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: patience stretched to breaking.

chapters.title: The Orchard Keeper's Daughter
chapters.summary: Wendell meets Nell Ashcombe, a young woman who has been tending the orchard alone in defiance of eviction orders. She doesn't trust him. POV: Nell's. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two people keeping the same vigil.

chapters.title: Bram's Confession
chapters.summary: Bram admits he helped sabotage the clock on Hale's orders years ago and has regretted it ever since; the letter was his penance. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: shame and the hope that a young stranger can undo an old wrong.

chapters.title: The Founders' Feast
chapters.summary: Hale hosts a feast unveiling Vey's draft history; the orchard keepers appear in one flattering, falsified paragraph. Wendell says nothing and hates himself for it. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: complicity tasted and swallowed.

chapters.title: Nell's Ledger
chapters.summary: Nell shows Wendell her grandmother's planting ledger, an oral record of the keepers' stewardship, the only surviving counter-history. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: fragile pride in what memory can hold.

chapters.title: The First Threat
chapters.summary: Wendell's tools are stolen and a note warns him to finish the clock and leave. He suspects Hale but cannot prove it. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Necessity
chapters.summary: Nell and Wendell agree to work together: she knows the keepers' records, he knows the clock. Bram agrees to help despite his terror of Hale. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the first stirrings of found family.

chapters.title: Vey's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vey discovers an inconsistency in the archives he's been given and privately begins to suspect the record was doctored before he arrived. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: a professional's conscience waking.

chapters.title: The Escapement Problem
chapters.summary: Wendell realizes opening the hidden compartment requires rebuilding the escapement entirely, a feat his master always said was beyond apprentices. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: self-doubt against necessity.

chapters.title: The Eviction Notice
chapters.summary: Hale serves Nell formal eviction papers, timed to clear the orchard before the history's publication. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: the machinery of power grinding toward her home.

chapters.title: Bram's Bargain
chapters.summary: Bram confronts Hale, offering silence in exchange for Nell's tenancy; Hale agrees, revealing he already knows about the letter. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: an old man's courage arriving too late to be clean.

chapters.title: The Watchmaker's Lesson
chapters.summary: In a flashback chapter, Wendell remembers his master teaching him that a clock is honest because it cannot lie about time. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: understanding that truth-keeping is his inheritance after all.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Mechanism
chapters.summary: Wendell begins the escapement rebuild with Nell keeping watch; they find the compartment's lock keyed to a specific gear tooth. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Stolen Ledger
chapters.summary: The keepers' ledger is stolen from Nell's cottage; she blames herself and nearly gives up. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: despair, and Wendell's clumsy, sincere comfort.

chapters.title: Vey's Offer
chapters.summary: Vey privately approaches Wendell, admitting his doubts and offering to print the true record if Wendell can produce evidence before publication. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: an enemy becoming a possible ally.

chapters.title: The Gear Tooth
chapters.summary: The keying gear is a unique part Wendell must machine from scratch, using Bram's old patterns; Nell recognizes the pattern as her grandfather's design. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the past literally fitting into the present.

chapters.title: Hale's History of Kindness
chapters.summary: Hale invites Wendell to dinner and tells a moving, false story of the town's founding, testing whether Wendell will accept the comfortable lie. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Wendell declines Hale's final offer of the permanent post, knowing the apprenticeship and his reputation will be destroyed. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the cost of truth counted and paid willingly.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone wrecks the clock's main train overnight; Bram is found injured nearby, and Hale's men arrest him for the vandalism. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: rage and guilt, the trap sprung.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Hearing
chapters.summary: At Bram's hearing, Wendell testifies about the original sabotage, but without the hidden records his word counts for nothing against Hale's. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the law revealed as another mechanism, and a broken one.

chapters.title: Nell's Stand
chapters.summary: Nell publicly reads her family's planting ledger on the courthouse steps, and a dozen townspeople quietly admit they remember the keepers. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: memory finding its voice in numbers.

chapters.title: The Last Tooth
chapters.summary: Working around the clock, Wendell finishes the keying gear as the publication deadline approaches. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Compartment Opens
chapters.summary: The hidden chamber opens: inside are the original founding registry, the keepers' land grants, and Odile Fen's sworn deposition naming Hale's grandfather as the forger. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: awe, then cold fear of what comes next.

chapters.title: The Clock Runs True
chapters.summary: Wendell restarts the master clock, and its corrected chimes ring across Marrowgate, drawing the town to the observatory. POV: multiple, brief. Emotional beat: the town forced to look up and listen.

chapters.title: The Confrontation
chapters.summary: Hale arrives with men to seize the records; Vey, choosing his conscience, reads the deposition aloud before the assembled town. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: the climax, a public reckoning that cannot be unpublished.

chapters.title: The Magistrate Reconsiders
chapters.summary: The town magistrate, facing the crowd, releases Bram and suspends the eviction pending a full inquiry into the land grants. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, but arriving.

chapters.title: Hale's Fall
chapters.summary: Hale's allies abandon him as the inquiry widens; he offers Wendell one last private deal and is refused. POV: Hale. Emotional beat: a powerful man discovering he was only ever renting his power.

chapters.title: The Inquiry
chapters.summary: The land grants are verified; the orchard terraces are returned to the keepers' heirs, with Nell named steward. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: vindication that feels less like victory than like coming home.

chapters.title: The Master's Letter
chapters.summary: Wendell receives a letter from his old master: the apprenticeship is revoked, but enclosed is a journeyman's certificate, signed in advance, for the escapement work alone. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: a door closing and a truer one opening.

chapters.title: The Planting
chapters.summary: In spring, Wendell, Nell, Bram, and a handful of townspeople replant the first orchard terrace together. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: found family rooted in shared labor.

chapters.title: The True History
chapters.summary: Vey publishes the corrected history with the registry reproduced in full; he credits Odile Fen and the keepers by name. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: the record set straight, on the record, ahead of the victors.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Wendell sets his pocket watch by the master clock and stays; the final image is the orchard in blossom, the clock striking true, and a family that chose him keeping time together. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: belonging, earned and kept.
